newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, supported by strength from packers looking for hogs to fill near-term slaughter needs, hog dealers and packer buyers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at the plant door, sources there said.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and $56.00 to $56.50, with the possibility of $57.00 at plants, Illinois sources said.
Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and $56.50 to $57.00 at plants, dealers there said.
However, Indiana hog prices could weaken as packers finish buying hogs they need for weekend slaughter operations, they said.
At least one major packer indicated it had plenty of hogs following a rush of early marketings in the Indiana market, one dealer said.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $57.00 at plants.
